FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: The HIL detection probability in §6 is mathematically inconsistent with its own symbol semantics because \(p_{H,j,k}\) is indexed by flaw class \(k\), but the defining formula is not. The appendix states
\[
p_{H,j,k}=\min\left(1, f_k(E,M)\prod_s(1+\lambda_sV_s)\right)
\]
and then defines
\[
f_k(E,M)=E(\alpha+(1-\alpha)M).
\]
But \(f_k\) contains no \(k\)-dependent term at all, and the product term is likewise not indexed by \(k\). So despite the notation, the model actually implies \(p_{H,j,k}=p_{H,j}\) for all flaw classes. That contradicts the surrounding prose, which motivates class-sensitive detection and later claims compatibility with class-specific diversity \(d_{H,j,k}\). As written, the HIL stream has no class-specific sensitivity beyond \(d_{H,j}\), making the \(k\) index on \(p_{H,j,k}\) misleading and the per-class combined coverage less expressive than claimed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove the class index and define \(p_{H,j}\) if human detection is intended to be class-invariant, or add an explicit class-sensitive term, e.g. \(p_{H,j,k}=\min(1, g_k\,E(\alpha+(1-\alpha)M)\prod_s(1+\lambda_{s,k}V_{s,k}))\), where \(g_k\) or \(\lambda_{s,k}\) encode class-specific human sensitivity. Then update \(C_H(k)\) and the prose accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The Bayesian calibration example table in §6 is numerically inconsistent with the stated posterior formula and prior. The appendix defines
\[
E^*(t)=\frac{a_0+\sum \text{catches}}{a_0+b_0+\sum \text{trials}}
\]
with \(a_0=b_0=2\), then gives posterior means like 0.357 after 1 review and 0.588 after 3 reviews for a “true rate 0.55”. Under a Beta-Binomial model, posterior means depend on integer counts of catches and trials, not directly on a continuous “true rate”. With \(a_0=b_0=2\), after 1 Bernoulli trial the only possible posterior means are \(2/5=0.4\) or \(3/5=0.6\), not 0.357. Likewise after 3 trials the possible posterior means are \(2/7,3/7,4/7,5/7\), none of which equal 0.588. So the table cannot have been generated by the stated formula under the stated prior and trial definition.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Regenerate the table from a fully specified simulation protocol: define what counts as a trial, how many Bernoulli opportunities per review, and whether entries are expected posterior means under simulation rather than exact posteriors after integer observations. If these are simulation averages, label them as Monte Carlo expectations and describe the simulation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: The HIL calibration metric \(\kappa=1-|E_{\text{claimed}}-E^*(t)|\) is underspecified at small \(t\) because \(E^*(t)\) is always defined, but its interpretation as a calibration score is unstable before any or enough trials exist. With \(t=0\), the posterior is just the prior mean \(a_0/(a_0+b_0)\), so \(\kappa\) measures agreement with the prior, not calibration against evidence. The text later discusses convergence “by approximately five reviews,” but the metric itself is presented without a domain guard. This creates an edge-case inconsistency: a reviewer can appear highly calibrated before any empirical evidence exists.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit guard such as “\(\kappa\) is advisory only for \(t<t_{\min}\), undefined for \(t=0\), or reported with a low-confidence tag until the posterior effective sample size exceeds a threshold.” Alternatively define \(\kappa(t)\) but require a separate credibility condition before acting on it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: The “Relationship to Other Extensions” claim in §8.6 that “\(F_n\) is a special case when \(n\) agents = 1 (no emergence possible)” is mathematically wrong as written because \(F_n\) and \(Y_{\text{composite}}\)-based emergence measure different objects. \(F_n\) is a detection coverage model over flaw classes and passes; §8 defines cognitive-yield constructs \(Y(t)\), \(Y_{\text{composite}}(t)\), and emergence inequalities. Setting the number of agents to 1 eliminates emergence, but it does not reduce the §8 system to \(F_n\). At most it reduces \(Y_{\text{composite}}\) to \(Y_1\), not to a coverage functional over \(p_{ik},d_{ik},w_k\). This is a category error between detection coverage and cognitive yield.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the statement with something like: “When \(n=1\), emergence metrics collapse to the single-agent cognitive-yield case \(Y_{\text{composite}}=Y_1\). This is complementary to, not reducible to, \(F_n\).”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: §8.1 defines round-level verification rate as
\[
\bar v(r)=\frac{\text{verified findings}}{\text{total findings at round }r},
\]
while §7.9 defines capability fingerprint \( \bar v \) as “Mean verification score — all findings from this model.” These are different quantities: one is round-local, the other model-global or condition-global. The notation reuses the same symbol without disambiguation, and §8.3 then uses “post-feedback \(\gamma\) increases or \(\bar v\) increases” without clarifying which \(\bar v\) is meant. This is more than cosmetic because the metacognitive improvement criterion depends on the exact aggregation window.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename the round-local metric to \(\bar v_r\) or \(v^{(r)}\), and keep the fingerprint component as \(\bar v_m\) or \(\bar v_{\text{all}}\). Update §8.1, §8.3, §7.9, and the notation summary.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: The “Convergence guarantee” language in §7.4 is mathematically overstated. The appendix says “As \(t\to T\), the remaining estimate \(\to 0\)” and gives a verified finite-horizon example. But that only shows the estimator’s remainder term vanishes as the analysis horizon closes; it does not establish convergence of the estimator to the true total analytical value except trivially at \(t=T\), where the future horizon is zero by construction. Calling this a convergence guarantee suggests stronger predictive validity than the formula provides.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rephrase to “terminal consistency” or “boundary condition correctness”: the remaining-estimate term vanishes as \(t\to T\), so \(\hat V(t,T)\) matches observed cumulative value at the horizon. Avoid calling this a convergence guarantee unless a separate proof of estimator consistency is supplied.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The code’s `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` is wired inconsistently with its own parser-yield and cost-per-finding logic. The method explicitly requires `response_time` and `response_chars` to detect parser-yield anomalies and cost-per-finding spikes, but `DynamicManager.process_round()` calls it as:
```python
model_diags = self.health_monitor.record_model_round(mid, fc, failed)
```
using only defaults `response_time=0.0` and `response_chars=0`. That means the parser-yield condition `response_chars > tau_chars and finding_count == 0` and the cost-per-finding spike logic cannot fire in normal orchestration flow. This is a model-to-code disconnect for the appendix’s \( \phi_i \) / parser-yield concept and the code’s claimed autonomous remediation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass actual response metadata from `responses[mid]`, e.g.
```python
resp = responses.get(mid)
self.health_monitor.record_model_round(
    mid, fc, failed,
    response_time=resp.response_time if resp else 0.0,
    response_chars=len(resp.content) if resp else 0,
)
```
and add a regression test showing parser-yield diagnosis fires on a long unparsed response.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes the system-level diminishing-returns yield from a flattened list of all members of cumulative equivalence classes:
```python
cum_findings_flat.extend(ec.members)
...
y = len(cumulative_findings) * h_bar
```
But equivalence classes are intended to deduplicate semantically same findings across models/rounds. Flattening all members destroys that deduplication and makes \(Y^{(\le r)}\) scale with repeated reports of the same class. That conflicts with the mathematical role of equivalence classes in convergence analysis and with §7.3’s intended cognitive-yield interpretation. If three models restate one issue, the code counts three findings in yield instead of one class-level discovery. This is distinct from previously reported “wrong aggregation target” issues: the specific inconsistency is between class-based deduplication and later member-level yield counting inside the same pipeline.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define system yield on deduplicated classes, not raw members. For example, use
\[
Y^{(\le r)} = |F^{(\le r)}_{\text{classes}}|\cdot \bar H_{\text{class}}^{(\le r)}
\]
with class-level abstraction aggregated per equivalence class, or explicitly state that yield intentionally counts support multiplicity and then align the appendix to that choice.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: The notation summary omits several symbols that become operationally important in the appendix’s own formulas: \(a_0,b_0\) in the Beta prior for \(E^*(t)\), \(FNR_i,TNR_i,TPR_i,FPR_i\) in §7.8, \(Y_{\text{union}}(t)\), and \( \bar H_{\text{union}}(t)\). Some are inferable, but the omission matters because the document presents itself as a formal supplement with a notation table intended to stabilise symbol meaning. The missing verifier-rate symbols are especially problematic because they drive the numeric weight table.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Extend the notation summary to include \(a_0,b_0,TPR_i,FPR_i,TNR_i,FNR_i,Y_{\text{union}}(t),\bar H_{\text{union}}(t)\), and any other symbols used in displayed equations but absent from the table.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: The reduction claim in §4 is too strong: “When \(s_k=w_k\), \(L_n\) reduces to \(R_n\).” This is only true if the weighting conventions are identical in role and normalisation. But §4’s motivation explicitly separates severity \(s_k\) from coverage weighting, while \(R_n\) is defined as a weighted average across classes using \(w_k\). If \(s_k\) is interpreted as expected harm in physical units (cost, loss, fatalities), then even setting its numeric values equal to current \(w_k\) does not preserve the semantics of \(R_n\) as a residual-risk score unless one also adopts the same scale and interpretation. The statement is algebraically true only under an identification of units and normalisation that the prose had just argued against.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Qualify the claim: “Algebraically, \(L_n\) equals \(R_n\) when \(s_k\) is chosen to equal the same normalised class weights \(w_k\); semantically this corresponds to collapsing severity and weighting back into one dimension.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE
